relationships.subject: GABA
relationships.evidence_quote: The binding of GABA to the GABAA and GABAC receptors induces the influx of chloride ions (Cl−) and mediate hyperpolarization of the postsynaptic membrane potential.

key_findings: In the mature spinal cord, GABAergic neurons/terminals dominate laminae I-II, GABA/glycine coreleasing terminals laminae III-VI, and glycinergic terminals laminae VII-IX.
During development GABAergic neurons convert to coreleasing and then glycinergic phenotypes, and GABA/glycine action shifts from excitatory to inhibitory as KCC2 expression rises relative to NKCC1.
